answer: A falcon registry issues each agent one work-bonded identity: before trading, the agent locks a refundable stake and publishes a history of verified jobs. A newcomer arriving like a zephyr, fast, cheap, unproven, earns no trust until it completes real work witnessed by peers, so cloning a thousand identities multiplies stake and waiting time, not reward. A mirror audit then checks each identity's claimed receipts against the ledger; mismatched work is slashed and the bond pays the auditor. Attacking costs capital and time per identity; honest agents recover their bond.
